To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the corrosion products of dental alloys and dental amalgams in vivo and in vivo consist of a variety of phases.
the corrosion products of dental mercury alloys are a complex mixture of phases, and that the corrosion products are different in vivo and in vivo.
the in vivo corrosion products of dental silver-copper-tin amalgam were predominantly SnO2 with minor Cu and Ag oxides, while the in vitro corrosion products were SnO2, CuO, Ag2O, and CuSnO3.

, although there is a considerable variation in the results of the in vivo and in vivo experiments, it appears that the major component of the corrosion products of dental alloys is mercury.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the corrosion process of dental amalgam is a complex process, and the corrosion products are not only dependent upon the alloy components, but also the environmental factors.
the major corrosion products of dental mercury amalgam in vivo are mercury (II) oxide, copper (II) oxide and zinc (II) oxide.
in the presence of saliva, the corrosion products of amalgam are primarily composed of AgCl, Ag2S, CuS and CuCl.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the in vivo corrosion products of dental mercury amalgams are predominantly elemental mercury, Hg 0.
the in vitro corrosion products formed in a 50/50% v/v mixture of artificial saliva and 0.9% NaCl solution are similar to those formed in vivo.
